ui.h: AI incidents in education and among young people
ui.lede: Verified cases from around the world in which AI harmed students, children, teenagers or the people and institutions that teach them, with the statistics, case studies and prevention measures that ministries, schools, universities and parents can act on.
ui.protect: Child protection: no child victim and no child perpetrator is named on this site. A young person is named only when their family made the name public in court or in mainstream media.
ui.k_school: Happened in a school or university
ui.s_year_h: Cases per year, by where they happened
ui.s_year_c: Each case is counted once, by the year it was first reported. Where it happened is kept separate from who was involved: a teenager harmed by a chatbot at home counts as a young person, not as a school incident.
ui.s_age_h: Age of the young people involved
ui.s_geo_c: Countries with the most case files. Counts reflect where incidents are reported and researched, so they understate countries with less media coverage in the languages we monitor.
ui.cs_c: Selected cases, each with what went wrong and what would have helped, based on the prevention guidance below.
ui.prev_c: Practical measures from education authorities, child-safety regulators and international bodies, grouped by risk. Each names who should act and the guidance it comes from.
ui.risk_staff_impersonation: Fakes and impersonation of teachers and school leaders
ui.risk_misfiring_tools: AI safety and monitoring tools that misfire
ui.laws_c: Examples of laws that criminalise sexual deepfakes of minors or regulate AI in education.
ui.method: How cases are included: a verified case file appears here when a person under 25 was harmed or involved, or when it happened in a school, university or education service. Each case records separately whether a young person was involved, their age group and where it happened. Data:
ui.b_h: AI and young people: a briefing for ministries of education
ui.b_lede: What the verified record shows about AI incidents affecting students, children, teenagers and schools worldwide, and what education authorities can do now.
ui.b_open: Open the briefing for ministries (print or save as PDF)
ui.b_f2: Harm reaches young people inside and outside school: {school} cases happened in schools and {uni} in universities, while {online} happened online and {home} at home. Prevention therefore has to reach families and online platforms, not only classrooms.
ui.b_f3: Teenagers are the most affected group: {teen} of the {n} cases involving a young person concern 13 to 17 year olds.
ui.b_f4: Much of the harm comes from tools that are free and easy to use: apps that turn a photo into a nude image, voice cloning, and general chatbots that are not designed for children. Several countries have already changed their laws in response.
ui.b_school_h: What every school should have in place
ui.b_about: Prepared by AI Threat Watch from its verified case files and from guidance published by education authorities, child-safety regulators and international bodies, as of {date}. Figures cover publicly reported cases that meet the registry's inclusion rule, so they show the pattern of harm, not its total size.
